svg.title: Soft Proof of Funds Acceptance Funnel
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-proof-of-funds-acceptance; chapter number: 6; chart type: funnel; title: Soft Proof of Funds Acceptance Funnel; subtitle: How listing agents respond to a soft letter, and what operators do with holdouts; caption: Across 20 years of the agent model, Jerry Norton reports about 90% of agents accept a soft letter; the remaining holdouts get a contingency or a downgraded offer.; assumptions note: Values are normalized to 100 offers using Norton's about 90% versus about 10% split. Stages 4 and 5 are two competing practitioner responses to the same holdout group, not further attrition.; note: Attributed to Jerry Norton (Flipping Mastery TV), Steph Davis (FlipThisWholesaler), Brent Daniels (Wholesaling Inc) and Foreclosure University.; stages: label: Offers backed by a soft proof letter; value: 100; display: 100 offers (normalized base); conversion: Base; detail: Letters from local hard money lenders or Tailwind at $1.99 each or $9.99 a month; the name on the proof must match the name on the offer.; label: Listing agent accepts the soft letter; value: 90; display: About 90 of 100; conversion: About 90% accept; detail: Norton says a soft letter checks the box for most listing agents.; label: Holdouts demanding hard proof; value: 10; display: About 10 of 100; conversion: About 10% push back; detail: Agents tie bank statements to the buyer named on the offer.; label: Holdouts given a 5-7 day contingency; value: 10; display: Five-to-seven-day contingency; conversion: Norton's response; detail: Norton offers the contingency and fires agents who still reject soft letters.; label: Holdouts moved to a financed offer; value: 10; display: Financing contingency; conversion: Davis's response; detail: Steph Davis still makes the offer but uses a financing contingency.
